title: feat: Add `LazyFrame.pivot`
description:
This PR adds `LazyFrame.pivot` which is the same as `DataFrame.pivot` except that it mandates a `on_columns` arguments. It can be used to `pivot` when the values are known ahead of time.

This also adds that same `on_columns` arguments to `DataFrame.pivot` (except it is optional there).

From an implementation perspective, `pivot` will now dispatch to a `group_by` with aggregations instead of having a custom implementation. This was shown to generally consume less memory and be faster, as the generic `group_by` implementations are much better optimized and supported.

comments.author: ritchie46
comments.body: I am hesitant on this one. I'd like to see some of the benchmarks we did in the past before merging this.

comments.author: coastalwhite
comments.body:
Doing a few benchmarks on the m5 forecasting dataset, this refactored pivot seems to be faster than the old (2-3x). This effect is clear both when the pivot grows in the `x` or `y` direction.

Looking at the profile, it seems like this stems from a part of the `pivot` being badly threaded.

comments.author: ritchie46
comments.body: Can you include this benchmark as well? https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/2968

comments.author: coastalwhite
comments.body:
On that benchmark:

~Old: 06.52s elapsed (2.8GB max resident)~
~New: 04.92s elapsed (1.8GB max resident)~

*edit: sorry that included the time to build the data. This is just timing the pivot*

```
Old: 01.74s elapsed (2.8GB max resident)
New: 00.21s elapsed (1.8GB max resident) # 8x faster!
```

comments.author: alexander-beedie
comments.body:
Exciting! And also amusing as I have a [branch](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/compare/main...alexander-beedie:wip-explicit-pivot-cols?expand=1) I made last week in which I added an "on_columns" to `pivot`, with the exact same parameter name, haha... (Not a rewrite though, just a basic extension of what was already there, with no lazy functionality - feel free to grab some of the unit tests if any look useful, and I'll park it in favour of The Real Deal™ 😄)

Happy to test this out more when it's ready to roll, as I have some _big_ pivots over here that could really benefit from this (they currently crash out with unexpectedly high memory usage).
